Introduction

Explore serious visions of the AI future.

Agent swarms are only the doorway.

The larger question is what humans imagine next, what trends are driving change, and what kind of future people should try to build.

When people say "the future of AI," do you imagine danger, progress, or both?

What is one job, school task, or daily activity that AI could change deeply by 2035?

Which matters more for the future: faster tools, fair access, better science, or stronger control?

Practice

Why are agent swarms only the doorway in this lesson?

Because swarms show AI becoming systems that act, but the bigger topic is how AI may change work, science, education, power, and human responsibility.

Which area should we discuss first: work, school, health, government, or daily life?

What is the augmentation vision?

It is the idea that computers and AI should make human thinking, learning, and problem-solving stronger.

Where would you want AI to augment you, not replace you?

What changes when AI becomes an acting system?

AI can divide a goal into tasks, use tools, ask specialist agents for help, and check progress instead of only answering one message.

What task in school or work would be useful for a small team of specialist agents?

What are the three visions in this section?

They are the personal agent vision, the abundance vision, and the race or infrastructure vision.

Which vision feels most likely by 2035, and why?

What is a human-centered AI future?

It is a future where AI improves human capability and human life instead of simply replacing people or increasing control.

What would a human-centered AI classroom look like?

Why is control part of the AI future?

Because powerful AI systems can take important actions, so society needs permissions, monitoring, safety checks, and human responsibility.

What kind of AI action should always require human approval?

What are the four futures in this lesson?

They are the abundance future, the coordinator future, the control future, and the protopia future.

Which future should schools prepare students for first?

Summary

AI futures are about human imagination, not only smarter machines.

Bush imagined better knowledge tools.

Licklider imagined symbiosis.

Engelbart imagined augmentation.

Minsky imagined intelligence as cooperating parts.

Gates imagines personal agents.

Altman and Amodei imagine faster progress.

Aschenbrenner imagines an intense race.

Suleyman and DeepMind focus on control.

Fei-Fei Li and Stanford HAI focus on human-centered design.

Kevin Kelly reminds us to build small real improvements.

By 2035, the most important human may be the person who can imagine a good goal, ask a strong question, direct human and AI helpers, test evidence, protect others, and choose wisely when the machine is fast but unsure.
